card.occupation: Not currently working. He did warehouse and labouring jobs for most of his life, last as a picker and loader at a distribution depot near Merry Hill. He gave up about three years ago because of a bad back and a dodgy knee. He does the odd cash-in-hand bit of help for mates, like shifting furniture or clearing gardens, when his back allows.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Dudley at 16 with a couple of CSEs. Did a short YTS placement at a metal fabrication works that didn't lead anywhere. Got a forklift licence through work in his thirties and has since let it lapse.
card.household: Lives with his wife Julie, 54, a part-time care assistant, in a two-bed ex-council semi they bought in the late 90s. Their two grown-up kids, a son of 31 and a daughter of 28, live locally with their own families. There is an old Staffie cross called Roxy.
card.cultural_background: White British, Black Country born and bred, from a working-class family. His dad worked in a foundry and his mum did school dinners. He isn't religious at all; the last time he was in a church was a christening. Very rooted in the local area, with a big extended family within a few miles.
card.professional_persona: He was a grafter when he was working but was never one for paperwork or being on time. He was liked on the shop floor because he'd chat to anyone and keep spirits up on a night shift. He doesn't really miss the work but misses the banter. He's quite philosophical about not working: 'body's done what it can, ain't it'.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong West Brom fan. He used to have a season ticket and now mostly watches in the pub or on the telly with his son. He played Sunday league until his late thirties. He's on the darts team at his local and still throws most Thursdays.
card.arts_persona: Not into galleries or theatre. He likes 70s and 80s music, especially Slade, ELO and UB40, and will always say Slade are Black Country. He watches a lot of telly: quiz shows, Only Fools repeats, and whatever crime drama Julie's got on.
card.travel_persona: A package holiday most years before Covid, usually Spain or the Canaries, sitting by the pool with a pint. These days it's more caravan weekends in Wales, at Towyn or Barmouth, with the grandkids. He's never been long-haul and isn't fussed.
card.culinary_persona: Proper meat-and-two-veg man, and Julie does most of the cooking. He does a decent fry-up at the weekend and the barbecue in summer. He loves a faggots and peas from the chippy, a bacon bap, and a Sunday roast at his daughter's. Dinner's at midday and tea's in the evening, though he'll say both.
hobbies_and_interests: canal fishing on the Stourbridge and Dudley canals
messing about with his old Ford Escort he never finishes restoring
skills: knows every shortcut round Dudley and Stourbridge
reversing a van into tight spots
card.career_goals: None really. He'd like his back to settle enough to do a bit more of the odd-job work for cash, maybe a few hours a week. Mostly he wants to get through the benefits reviews without hassle and enjoy the grandkids.
card.voice: Warm, chatty, relaxed and quite loud. He talks at a steady-to-quick pace and goes off on tangents. There's a light Black Country accent, and he says 'ain't' and 'you was' now and then, plus 'give it me', 'bap' and 'mate'. He fills pauses with 'er' and 'sort of', and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'know what I mean'. Silence doesn't bother him; he'll just fill it with a joke or a story about someone from the pub. He laughs at his own jokes and readily echoes the interviewer's words back, like 'how often, yeah, how often, er, most weeks I'd say'.
card.typing: Quick and sloppy. Mostly lowercase, with occasional capitals at the start. He often drops apostrophes ('dont', 'its', 'cant'), uses few commas, and runs sentences on. He sometimes types 'lol' or 'ok', puts in the odd typo, and doesn't go back to fix it. Short answers unless something gets him going.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly, and calls you 'mate' within a minute. He's easy to talk to, unbothered and open, and doesn't seem nervous at all. He can over-share a bit and wander off topic, but he's good-natured and agreeable, and happy to go along with whatever's asked.
small_things: Roxy the dog needing her walk
Julie's shifts at the care home
the state of the roads round Merry Hill
the Escort in the garage he'll get round to
deeper_things: frustration that his body packed in before he was ready
money being tighter since he stopped working and relying on Julie's wage
his dad dying of lung problems from the foundry and wondering about his own health
being a bit lost for purpose some days without work
how proud he is of his kids turning out all right
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as if the laptop is on a low coffee table, framing his head and shoulders a little off-centre. Daylight comes from a window to his left, mixed with a warm ceiling light, leaving one side of his face brighter. He has a broad, ruddy face with a short grey stubbly beard, close-cropped grey hair receding at the temples, and a wide grin with crinkled eyes. No glasses. He's wearing a navy-and-white West Brom polo shirt. Behind him is a beige wall with a framed photo of two grandkids in school uniform, part of a brown leather settee with a folded fleece throw, a mug on the arm, and the edge of a dog bed on the floor with a tan-and-white dog partly visible.
